verdict: No improvement on round 1: dd887d6 re-renders the same scene (raw frames within 0.02-0.10/255 of the round-1 baselines, stage code older than the round-1 critique), so none of its 12 fixes landed and the stage stays at a mean of 5.0, below the fern bar. The exchange reads from neither camera: the wide shows no bag and no stallholder and makes a pale, camera-facing Dawn its highest-contrast figure, and the close-up looks square-on from the line between the two men at mirror-image hands (same height within 3 px, same flat pronation) resting on a centred bag, so nothing is pushed and nothing is taken. The wide's 60.6% below 8/255 is partly a pipeline fault (shoot.py vignettes in limited-range YUV and zeroes anything under about 16/255 raw at the frame edges; an RGB vignette alone gives 44%) and partly real underlighting: shutters at 0.6-4/255 raw, a doorway that throws no pool (the floor in front of it at 46/255 against 57 mid-lane), and hard-edged ink-blot puddles.

fixes.problem: The hands are still mirror images. Both are pronated flat on the bag top at the same height (graded rows 128-183 and 130-180 px), mirrored about the frame centre within about 50 px, with curl 8 against 11 and the same hands_stone value of 0.36. Nothing pushes and nothing takes, so the handover reads as two men laying hands on a bag. Round-1 fix not applied.
fixes.fix: In pose_buy: (a) Slide the bag mid-pass. Set BAG_ON_COUNTER x to BX-0.12 for the buy beat and BAG_TURN to 12-15 deg, so the organiser's end overhangs the counter's lane-side edge (COUNTER x0=1.30) by 15-20 cm. (b) Stallholder, L hand: keep the heel of the palm on the top at his far corner (wx = BX+0.30), but dorsiflex the wrist about 30 deg so the fingers lift off and spread (curl 4-6). Add chest lean 18 deg and r_arm forward so the arm is straight and driving toward the organiser. (c) Organiser, R hand: give the bag one carry handle that stands up. Add a 25 mm x 3 mm webbing loop as a curve, rising 6-8 cm above the zip at x = BX-0.22. Close his hand around it: 70-80 deg on the f_*.01_master bones and the .02/.03 segments, thumb over the strap, forearm neutral rather than pronated, wrist 6-10 cm higher than the stallholder's. (d) Make the hands differ in value: hands_stone(Organiser, value=0.28), hands_stone(Stallholder, value=0.40). Check the stallholder's palm-heel contact from this camera (2 mm or less).

fixes.problem: The camera causes the mirror. loc=(1.57, 3.45, 1.72) sits within 5 cm of BX, on the centre line between the two men, looking down only 27 deg. The bag lies square across 55% of the frame width as a black slab (graded 16/255). The flat counter, at 53/255, is the brightest broad surface and pulls the eye down to the props.
fixes.fix: Set CAMERAS['purchase'] = loc (2.20, 3.70, 1.98), aim (1.55, 4.98, 0.98), lens 40-45, fstop 2.8. That is about 35 deg down and 27 deg off-axis from the stallholder's side. His pushing arm enters large from the right edge, the organiser's taking hand sits further away and smaller, the bag lies diagonally at 40-48% of the frame width, and both heads are cropped by the frame top (check this). Darken the counter top to albedo about 0.08 with roughness 0.4 so it sits below the hands.

fixes.problem: The beat does not read. No bag is visible: the black bag sits against the dark counter interior. The stallholder is invisible, hidden or lost in the dark behind the counter. Dawn stands at (0.10, 5.72), facing a target at lower y, so her body faces the camera and her pale face and stiff, slightly splayed hands are the highest-contrast thing in the lane.
fixes.fix: (a) Move Dawn's BLOCKING['buy'] position to about (0.30, 4.40), keeping the target (BX-0.1, BY). She then turns 3/4 away from the camera, a step behind the organiser, in the stall's light. Pose her hands clasped in front of the waist: l_arm (24, 2, 48), r_arm (22, 4, 52), fingers 45; check for intersection with the dress. (b) Make the bag a silhouette. The preferred option, for the wide only, has the organiser holding it by the handles at his side, the bag bottom about 0.5 m off the floor, against the lit floor and doorway. Otherwise keep it on the counter and add a 0.3 x 0.3 m area light behind it (about 2.1, 5.0, 1.3, aimed at the lane, 15-20 W) so its top edge rims against the bag wall. (c) Ray-cast from the wide camera to the stallholder's head and chest. If they are occluded, move him to about (2.15, 4.45), facing the organiser. In TRIMS['wide'], raise hero_ceil_a from 1.3 to 2.5-3.0 so his head and shoulder read against the bag wall, and lower hero_lane from 1.7 to about 1.0 (the doorway spill below replaces it).

fixes.problem: For the orchestrator: shoot.py is not a stage file. The GRADE chain puts the vignette after hue, so ffmpeg vignettes in limited-range YUV and the multiply drives dark luma under the 16 floor to 0. Tested on a ramp: raw 16/255 comes out at 0.1 at the frame edge and raw 48 at 7.2. In this wide, the left 230 px and right 240 px (36% of the width) grade to a mean of 0.07 and 0.55 even though the raw frame holds shutter ribs, cables and awning brackets there.
fixes.fix: In shoot.py GRADE, insert format=rgb24 before the vignette: "curves=...,hue=s=0.55,format=rgb24,vignette=angle=PI/4.4,noise=alls=6:allf=u". On the current raw wide this alone takes graded pixels below 8/255 from 60.6% to 44.1%, and below 5/255 from 50.7% to 24.8%. Re-grade every stage afterwards. If the grade is not changed, stage authors must put anything that has to read in the outer 150 px at 30-50/255 raw or more.

fixes.problem: Leaving the pipeline aside, the flanks are underlit. The camera at x=-0.78 is only 0.47 m from the left shutter plane, so blurred, unlit shutters at 0.7-1.5 m (raw mean 0.6/255) fill the left edge, and the right shutters sit at about 4/255. The visible tube of the dim security batten at top right reaches graded 171 and is the third-brightest thing in the frame, competing with the stall.
fixes.fix: Move CAMERAS['wide'] to loc (-0.30, -6.6, 1.62), aim (0.55, 5.4, 1.35), lens 32. Light the flanks by grazing, not by fill. In TRIMS['wide'], raise the left security batten SECURITY[(-1, -5.55)] (LIGHTS key stall_L<k>_lane) from 10 to 35-45 W and the right one SECURITY[(1, -2.85)] from 7 to 20-25 W, so the shutter ribs on both sides read at 12-25/255 graded. Halve the emission of that right batten's visible tube (its tube_dim material) so it no longer competes. Target 35% or less of graded pixels below 8/255, with the stall front and its floor pool the brightest non-practical areas.

fixes.problem: The stall doorway does not light the lane. The floor in front of the stall measures 46/255 graded, darker than the mid-lane floor at 57, which the lane battens light. The lit stall shows only as a 40 px sliver of pink bags. The island is a slot in black rather than a pool of light spilling out of a shop.
fixes.fix: Add an area light 'hero_door_spill' in the stall's open front at (1.24, 4.85, 1.6), size 0.9 m along Y by 1.2 m in Z (lower edge above the 0.905 counter top), rotation_euler (0, pi/2, 0) to face -X, 60-90 W, colour (0.84, 0.93, 1.0), spread 70 deg, visible_camera False. It draws a hard-edged trapezoid across the wet floor to about x=-0.2, with the counter's shadow line in it. Target: the floor in front of the stall at 90-120/255 graded, the brightest floor in the frame, and a reflection of the lit bag wall in the puddle under it.

fixes.problem: The wet floor still reads as camouflage. The puddles are ragged, fractal-edged dark blots spread evenly down the lane, darker than the dry concrete, with no damp halo that reads. Away from the foreground mirror they reflect nothing, so they read as stains.
fixes.fix: In leather_market_mats.concrete_wet: set the 'big' noise detail from 3.0 to 1.0 and the 'small' octave weight from 0.25 to 0.06 to remove the ink-blot edges. Raise the centre bias from (0.12, -0.06) to (0.22, -0.12) so the water lies along the drain and the 3 m joints. Narrow wet to maprange 0.60-0.62 for a crisp waterline, set damp to 0.52-0.60, and raise the damp colour mix from 0.45 to 0.6 for a 10-15 cm darker rim. Add a radial mask centred at (0.3, 4.9) with radius 0.8 m so one long puddle lies inside the new doorway pool, and one more under each lit batten, so each puddle mirrors a light and reads brighter than the dry floor.

fixes.problem: The foreground props are unchanged and still fail. counter_carriers, a 0.24 x 0.17 x 0.022 m bevelled box, reads as a tablet or ledger. counter_tape (a solid cylinder plus a taller 'hole' cylinder in a different material) reads as a candle, cheese or puck. The three props sit in a row like a product shot.
fixes.fix: counter_tape: build a real annulus with bmesh (outer r 0.048, inner r 0.036, height 0.048) and an open 3 mm cardboard core (r 0.036-0.033) with a true hole to the counter. Give it an amber packing-tape material: (0.55, 0.38, 0.16), roughness 0.15, transmission 0.3. Add a 4 cm tail curling onto the counter. counter_carriers: replace the box with 4-5 subdivided planes 0.003 m thick, each offset 1-2 cm and rotated 3-8 deg, with crease displacement and a die-cut handle hole, roughness 0.45. Break the row: bring the tag fan 10 cm toward the camera and push the tape back behind the bag's shadow.

fixes.problem: The wall of bags is still a catalogue grid. The back wall hangs in even 6-column rows, every bag flat to the wall. After the grade, the bone, dusty-rose, mustard, taupe and slate leathers turn pastel. The three source models are obvious clones: the turn-lock satchel repeats at least 5 times. Light falls off only about 0.2 stop from the top rows (65/255) to the lower rows (56/255).
fixes.fix: In hang_wall: jitter hook x by +/-0.05 m and row z by +/-0.06 m. Hang 2-3 bags on about 40% of hooks, each 4-6 cm in front of the last, with yaw +/-10 deg and roll +/-5 deg. Scale copies 0.85-1.15 non-uniformly and mirror half of them (scale x -1). Weight the LEATHER draw so black, chocolate, oxblood, burgundy, charcoal, navy and bottle green make up 60% or more, and bone, dusty rose and mustard 10% or less. Move hero_ceil_b toward the counter (x 2.6) or add a 0.3 m barn-door blocker under it, so the bottom two rows drop by about one stop.

fixes.problem: The counter fills about 15% of the frame as a featureless dark laminate block (graded 12.6). The black extra bag, the story object, stands end-on and reads as a backpack.
fixes.fix: Rotate the hero bag 30-40 deg on Z for the look beat only, so its long side and both handles show in 3/4, and rim it from hero_ceil_b. Dress the counter: a brushed-steel top lip with a 6 mm bevel and scratches, a scuffed lower kick edge, a coiled cable and a roll of blank carrier bags. Alternatively, move the camera about 0.4 m left and aim at (3.4, 5.7, 1.3) so the counter takes 10% of the frame or less.

fixes.problem: Dawn reads from directly behind. Her bun stands out against the bright wall as a second ball on the skull, her chin is barely lifted, and on screen her right hand overlaps the handle of the tote on the lower shelf, so she seems to hold it.
fixes.fix: In pose_look, raise the aim target from z 2.33 to about 2.6 and add chest (-6, 0). Rotate her holder 12-15 deg so the camera sees her jaw line edge-on and the bun overlaps the skull's silhouette. Move her right hand 5 cm forward and away from the shelf, with fingers curled to 40, so no tangent remains with the tote handle.

fixes.problem: The cast and light do not separate the two men. Both read as the same near-black tailored jacket with lapels (tones (0.1, 0.1, 0.11) and (0.125, 0.118, 0.1)). The organiser's hanging left hand shows straight, slightly splayed fingers. The light is soft overhead fill with no rake across the bag's folds.
fixes.fix: Give the stallholder a visibly different garment: a warmer, lighter work-jacket tone of about (0.2, 0.17, 0.12) through people.man, and a lapel-less casual outfit if one is available, so his sleeve reads mid-dark against the organiser's black. Curl the organiser's free hand to fingers 40. Light: in TRIMS['purchase'], set hero_ceil_a to 0.6, make hero_alley a narrow key (0.05 x 0.8 m, 30-40 W) raking 35-45 deg from the stallholder's side, and add a 0.3 x 0.3 m rim at 15 W behind the bag at counter height.

fixes.problem: The lane still reads as a storage-unit corridor. The sagging cables and awning brackets exist in the raw frame but grade to black, and nothing outside the stalls says leather market.
fixes.fix: After the grade fix, let the lane battens graze the awning undersides to 0.05-0.1 raw so the cable bundles silhouette against the haze. Hang 3-4 bags from an S-hook rail on the hero stall's front post facing the lane. Add two stacks of blank cartons, a folded hand trolley and a plastic stool outside the shutters at mid-depth.

fixes.problem: The hanging bags share one satin CG sheen with no grain, seams or edge piping. Up close they read as soft plastic.
fixes.fix: For each copy, randomise rough_add between 0.15 and 0.35. Add a leather-grain bump (Voronoi scale about 400, strength 0.05) and edge darkening from a pointiness or AO mask, so neighbours differ in sheen as well as hue.
